319441.title: The major-arcs conjecture for exceptional sets of additive problems
319441.statement:
Let ${\mathcal A},{\mathcal B}\subseteq {\mathbb N}$. Write $\overline{{\mathcal A}+{\mathcal B}}$ for the exceptional set associated with the sumset ${\mathcal A}+{\mathcal B}$, let $|\mathcal B|_0^N$ denote the number of elements of ${\mathcal B}$ up to $N$, and let $\widehat {\Upsilon}(\overline{{\mathcal A}+{\mathcal B}},{\mathcal B};N)$ be the corresponding exceptional-set counting function. **Major-arcs conjecture.** One has

$$
\widehat {\Upsilon}(\overline{{\mathcal A}+{\mathcal B}},{\mathcal B};N)\ll N^{\varepsilon-1}\left(\left|\overline{{\mathcal A}+{\mathcal B}}\right|_{2N}^{3N}|{\mathcal B}|_0^N\right)^2.
$$

This estimate is suggested by a heuristic application of the Hardy–Littlewood method and would quantify the expected improvement in exceptional-set estimates obtained by adding ${\mathcal B}$. The source presents it as a speculation rather than a proved result.
319441.source_name: Koichi Kawada and Trevor D. Wooley, “Relations between exceptional sets for additive problems”, arXiv:1001.2495 (2010).
319441.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.2495

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2010).

319494.title: Droms–Mellinger–Meyer dimension conjecture for projective-plane LDPC codes
319494.statement:
Let $q$ be an odd prime power, and let ${\mathbf B}$ and ${\mathbf B}_0$ be the incidence matrices of internal points versus secant lines and external points versus passant lines, respectively, in ${\mathrm{PG}}(2,q)$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{L}_0$ be their column $\mathbb F_2$-null spaces. **Droms–Mellinger–Meyer's conjecture.** The dimensions are

$$
\dim_{\mathbb F_2}(\mathcal{L})=\begin{cases}\frac{q^2-1}{4}-q,&q\equiv1\pmod4,\\frac{q^2-1}{4}-q+1,&q\equiv3\pmod4,
\end{cases}
$$

and

$$
\dim_{\mathbb F_2}(\mathcal{L}_0)=\begin{cases}\frac{q^2-1}{4},&q\equiv1\pmod4,\\frac{q^2-1}{4}+1,&q\equiv3\pmod4.
\end{cases}
$$

These formulas concern the dimensions of the four low-density parity-check codes constructed from submatrices of the point-line incidence matrix of ${\mathrm{PG}}(2,q)$. The article confirms this conjecture, so the claim is solved.
319494.source_name: Junhua Wu, “Proofs of Two Conjectures On the Dimensions of Binary Codes”, arXiv:1001.5077 (2011).
319494.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.5077

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of January 2010); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

320040.title: White's conjecture for lattice path polymatroids
320040.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a lattice path polymatroid. Its base ring is the polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[Y_m: m$ is a basis of $\Gamma]$, and its toric ideal is the kernel of the map

$$
\phi: \mathbb{C}[Y_m: m \text{ is a basis of }\Gamma] \longrightarrow \mathbb{C}[x_0,x_1,x_2,\ldots],
$$

defined by $\phi(Y_{m_1}Y_{m_2}\cdots Y_{m_t})=m_1m_2\cdots m_t$. A **symmetric exchange binomial** is a binomial $Y_mY_{m'}-Y_nY_{n'}$ obtained when $n$ and $n'$ are obtained from $m$ and $m'$ by a symmetric exchange. **White's conjecture, adapted for polymatroids.** The toric ideal of $\Gamma$ is generated by symmetric exchange binomials. The paper proves this statement for lattice path polymatroids, so it is solved in the stated class, although the broader polymatroid version is presented as an adaptation of White's conjecture.
320040.source_name: Jay Schweig, “Toric Ideals of Lattice Path Matroids and Polymatroids”, arXiv:1006.2560 (2010).
320040.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.2560

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of June 2010); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

320198.title: Symmetry and central-circuit conjectures for ({1,2,3},6)- and ({2,3},6)-spheres
320198.statement:
A $(\{1,2,3\},6)$-sphere is a sphere whose face sizes belong to $\{1,2,3\}$ and whose vertex degree is $6$; a $(\{2,3\},6)$-sphere is defined similarly with face sizes in $\{2,3\}$. A sphere is **$z$-knotted** or **$c$-knotted** when it has only one zigzag or only one central circuit, respectively. Its symmetry is denoted by the corresponding point-group symbol, and its $c$- and $z$-vectors record the lengths of its central circuits and zigzags.

**Symmetry and circuit conjecture.** (i) A $z$- or $c$-knotted $(\{1,2,3\},6)$-sphere, except Trifolium $C_{3v}$, has symmetry $C_1$, $C_2$, $C_3$, $D_2$ or $D_3$. (ii) A $(\{2,3\},6)$-sphere with only simple central circuits has symmetry $T_d$, $T_h$, $D_{6h}$, $D_{3d}$, $D_{2d}$, $D_{2h}$, $D_3$, $C_{2h}$ or $C_{3v}$. (iii) A $(\{1,2,3\},6)$-sphere of symmetry $D_{6h}$, $T_h$ or $T_d$ has only simple central circuits and zigzags. (iv) A $(\{2,3\},6)$-sphere of symmetry $T_d$ has $v=4x^2$ vertices, $c$-vector $(3x)^{4x}$ and $z$-vector $(6x)^{4x}$. (v) A $(\{2,3\},6)$-sphere of symmetry $T_h$ has $12x^2$ vertices, $c$-vector $(6x)^{6x}$ and $z$-vector $(12x)^{6x}$.

These assertions classify the possible symmetries and circuit structures in several highly symmetric or knotted families of discrete spheres. The supplied text gives no evidence that the conjecture has been proved or refuted.
320198.source_name: Michel Deza and Mathieu Dutour Sikiric, “(2,3, 6)-spheres and their generalizations”, arXiv:1007.4706 (2010).
320198.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.4706

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2010).

320265.title: Ross's sub-lattice conjecture for periodic framework rigidity
320265.statement: Let $\tilde{G}(\mathbf{p},\mathbf{L})$ be an infinitesimally rigid periodic framework with periodic graph $(\tilde{G},\varphi)$. Let $\Lambda<\mathbb{Z}^2$ be any sub-lattice, and define $(\tilde{G},\varphi')$ to be the periodic graph obtained by replacing the $\mathbb{Z}^2$-action $\varphi$ with the induced $\Lambda$-action $\varphi'$. **Ross's conjecture.** Then $\tilde{G}(\mathbf{p},\mathbf{L})$ is an infinitesimally rigid realization of the induced abstract periodic framework on $(\tilde{G},\varphi')$. Informally, this says that a generic rigid periodic framework remains rigid when the periodicity constraint is relaxed to a sub-lattice, enlarging the class of allowed motions. The conjecture concerns whether infinitesimal rigidity is preserved under passage from the original lattice to any sub-lattice; its resolution is not given here.
320265.source_name: Justin Malestein and Louis Theran, “Generic combinatorial rigidity of periodic frameworks”, arXiv:1008.1837 (2012).
320265.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.1837

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2010).

320916.title: Conjectured skeletons and non-adjacencies for partial metric and weighted quasi-metric cones
320916.statement:
Let $S(n,2)=2^{n-1}-1$ be the Stirling number counting partitions of an $n$-element set into two nonempty blocks. For a polyhedral cone, write ${\operatorname{Sk}}$ for its skeleton, $K_m$ for the complete graph on $m$ vertices, $K_{a,b}$ for the complete bipartite graph, and $+$ for disjoint union. Let $\text{\sl OCUT}_n$, $\text{\sl WQMET}_n$, and $0,1\text{-}\text{\sl dWMET}_n$ denote the corresponding cones used in the source; $\delta'(S)$ and $w'$ denote the indicated cut and weight vertices.

**Skeleton conjecture.** (i) ${{\operatorname{Sk}}}(\text{\sl OCUT}_n)=K_{2S(n,2)}$ and is a subgraph of ${{\operatorname{Sk}}}(\text{\sl WQMET}_n)$. (ii) The complement of ${{\operatorname{Sk}}}(0,1\text{-}\text{\sl dWMET}_n)$ is $K_{1,S(n,2)}+S(n,2)K_2$; its skeleton has diameter $2$, and all non-adjacencies are of the forms $(((0));(1))\nsim(\delta'(S);(0))$ and $(\delta'(S);w')\nsim(\delta'(S);w')$.

The claims concern the adjacency structure of skeleton graphs of cones of oriented cuts, weighted quasi-metrics, and discrete weighted metrics. The paper says that the proofs should be tedious but easy, but the supplied material gives no resolution evidence.
320916.source_name: Michel Deza, Elena Deza and Janoš Vidali, “Cones of Weighted and Partial Metrics”, arXiv:1101.0517 (2011).
320916.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.0517

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2011).

320917.title: Conjectured ridge graphs of partial metric and weighted quasi-metric cones
320917.statement:
Let $\text{\sl PMET}_n$ and $\text{\sl WQMET}_n$ be the partial-metric and weighted quasi-metric cones from the source, and let ${{\operatorname{Ri}}}$ denote their ridge graphs. The vertices $L_{ii}$, $M_{ij}$, and $Tr_{ij,k}$ are the corresponding facet classes; two $Tr$ facets **conflict** when they have values of different signs on a common position among their indexed coordinates.

**Ridge-graph conjecture.** (i) ${{\operatorname{Ri}}}(\text{\sl PMET}_n)$ has diameter $2$, with all non-adjacencies given by $L_{ii}\nsim M_{ik}$; $M_{ij}\nsim M_{ji},M_{ki},M_{jk},Tr_{ij,k}$; and $Tr_{ij,k}\nsim Tr_{i'j',k'}$ when they conflict. (ii) ${{\operatorname{Ri}}}(\text{\sl WQMET}_n)$ has diameter $2$ and is obtained from ${{\operatorname{Ri}}}(\text{\sl PMET}_n)$ by deleting the vertices $L_{ii}$.

These claims describe the full non-adjacency patterns in the ridge graphs of two families of polyhedral cones. The source calls the proofs tedious but easy and supplies no evidence that the conjectures have been resolved.
320917.source_name: Michel Deza, Elena Deza and Janoš Vidali, “Cones of Weighted and Partial Metrics”, arXiv:1101.0517 (2011).
320917.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.0517

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2011).

321074.title: Counting word-representable digraphs with a prescribed number of strong components
321074.statement: Let an $\ell$-word be a word of length $\ell$ over an $n$-letter alphabet, and suppose it has a unique factorisation into factors corresponding to alphabet-disjoint partitions. A word-graph is the digraph represented by such a word, and a strong component is a maximal strongly connected subdigraph. **Counting conjecture.** The number of $\ell$-words over an $n$-alphabet, with a unique factorisation, that represent word-graphs with $k$ strong components is the number of $n$-partitions of an $\ell$-set with $k$ disjoint proper subsets of parts whose union is a set of the form ${j,j+1,\ldots,j+m}$. Each such union is an alphabet-disjoint partition in the corresponding representational word and is a strong component in the corresponding word-graph. This is presented as possible future work extending the paper's enumeration of strongly connected word-graphs; the text does not provide a proof or establish the asserted enumeration.
321074.source_name: Edward J. L. Bell, Damon Berridge and Paul Rayson, “The strong-connectivity of word-representable digraphs”, arXiv:1102.0980 (2011).
321074.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.0980

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2011).

321624.title: Semi-Kotzig-frame double cover conjecture
321624.statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph. A **frame** of $G$ is a spanning subgraph $H$ such that the contraction $G/H$ is even. For a subgraph $H$, let $\overline{H}$ denote the graph obtained by suppressing all degree-$2$ vertices. A **semi-Kotzig frame** is a frame whose every non-circuit component has suppressed graph a semi-Kotzig graph. A **$6$-even-subgraph double cover** is a double cover consisting of six even subgraphs.

**Semi-Kotzig-frame conjecture.** Every bridgeless cubic graph with a semi-Kotzig frame has a $6$-even-subgraph double cover.

This strengthens the preceding Kotzig-frame conjecture by replacing Kotzig frames with the more general semi-Kotzig frames. The paper proves the result for semi-Kotzig frames with at most one non-circuit component, while the unrestricted statement remains open.
321624.source_name: Dong Ye and Cun-Quan Zhang, “Cycle Double Covers and Semi-Kotzig Frame”, arXiv:1105.5190 (2011).
321624.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.5190

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2011).

322500.title: Universal rotor-router classification conjecture
322500.statement: A **rotor type** is a finite sequence of directions; a rotor type is **palindromic** if it reads the same forwards and backwards, and **block-repetitive** if it is a concatenation of uniform blocks of a common length. A rotor type is **boppy** if it is palindromic or block-repetitive, and **unboppy** otherwise. Let $\mathbf{ROT}$ be the class of all rotor types, $\mathbf{U}$ the class of universal rotors, and $\mathbf{BOP}$ the class of boppy rotors. Complements are taken in $\mathbf{ROT}$. **Universal rotor classification conjecture.** As classes of rotor types, $\mathbf{U}=\overline{\mathbf{BOP}}$. This would classify precisely the nonuniversal rotor types as the palindromic and block-repetitive ones; the statement is presented as a conjecture, and its general status is not resolved in the supplied text.
322500.source_name: Xiaoyu He, “On the Classification of Universal Rotor-Routers”, arXiv:1111.1459 (2011).
322500.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.1459

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2011).

322777.title: The equal-block minimizer conjecture for multipartite flag-complex constructions
322777.statement:
Let $1\leq p<k<r$ be integers, and let $m,n$ be real numbers satisfying

$$
m>{r\choose k}n^{k/r}.
$$

Define $w(i)=k$ if $i\leq k$ and $w(i)=r$ if $i>k$. Consider positive real numbers $a_1^k,\dots,a_k^k,a_1^r,\dots,a_r^r$ satisfying

$$
n=a_1^r a_2^r\dots a_r^r,
$$

$$
m=\sum_{i_1<i_2<\dots<i_k}a_{i_1}^{w(i_k)}a_{i_2}^{w(i_k)}\dots a_{i_k}^{w(i_k)},
$$

with $a_i^k\geq a_j^k$ whenever $i<j$ and $a_j^i\geq a_j^k$ whenever $i<k$.

**Equal-block minimizer conjecture.** The unique choice of constants minimizing

$$
\sum_{i_1<i_2<\dots<i_p}a_{i_1}^{w(i_p)}a_{i_2}^{w(i_p)}\dots a_{i_p}^{w(i_p)}
$$

is also the unique choice satisfying

$$
a_1^k=\dots=a_k^k=a_1^r=\dots=a_k^r>a_{k+1}^r=\dots=a_r^r.
$$

This conjecture identifies the proposed extremal pattern for minimizing lower-dimensional faces after fixing the numbers of $k$- and $r$-faces. It is presented as an explanation for why equal parameters within the relevant blocks are a natural construction, but its general validity remains open.
322777.source_name: Andrew Frohmader, “How to construct a flag complex with a given face vector”, arXiv:1112.6061 (2011).
322777.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.6061

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2011).

376549.title: The claw-free hard-core zero conjecture
376549.statement: Let $G$ be a finite claw-free graph, meaning that it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{1,3}$. Let $Z(w)$ be the hard-core lattice-gas partition function of $G$. **Hamidoune–Stanley conjecture.** All zeros of $Z(w)$ are negative real. This would extend the Heilmann–Lieb real-negative-zero theorem from line graphs to all claw-free graphs; the source presents it as a conjecture and gives no resolution.
376549.source_name: Alan D. Sokal, “A Personal List of Unsolved Problems Concerning Lattice Gases and Antiferromagnetic Potts Models”, arXiv:cond-mat/0004231 (2000).
376549.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0004231

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2000). “For planar graphs, it is an open question.”

376947.title: Induced-ridge-graph conjecture for m-hemimetric cones
376947.statement: Let $HM_n^m$, $NHM_n^m$, and $P_n^m$ be the corresponding cones of $m$-hemimetrics, and let the ridge graph of a cone have the facets as vertices, with adjacency when two facets meet in a ridge. **Induced-ridge-graph conjecture.** The ridge graph of $HM_n^m$ is an induced subgraph of the ridge graph of $NHM_n^m$, and the ridge graph of $NHM_n^m$ is an induced subgraph of the ridge graph of $P_n^m$. In $NHM_n^m$, the two vertex orbits are $F_1$ and $F_2$, consisting respectively of $(n-m-1)\binom{n}{m+1}$ simplex inequalities and $\binom{n}{m+1}$ nonnegativity inequalities. The conjecture concerns the general inclusion pattern of these ridge graphs; the source gives computational observations for small parameters but no general proof.
376947.source_name: M. Deza and I. Rosenberg, “Small cones of m-hemimetrics”, arXiv:math/0005270 (2001).
376947.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0005270

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2000).

376968.title: Polynomiality conjecture for the singular-point contribution on ${\cal M}_N$
376968.statement:
Let $N$ be odd, and let

$$
d_{M'}=\sum\limits_{i+j=N,\ i\,\text{ is even}}d^{i,j}_N(k,k,k;q,z)
$$

be the contribution associated with the singular point on ${\cal M}_N$. **Polynomiality conjecture.** Then

$$
d_{M'}=\frac{P_N(q,z)}{\prod\limits_{i=1}^N(1-q^{-i}z^{-1})},
$$

where $P_N(q,z)$ is a polynomial. This statement is proposed to describe the contribution of the singular point on ${\cal M}_N$; the supplied text gives no evidence that the claim has been proved or disproved.
376968.source_name: B. Feigin and S. Loktev, “On finitization of the Gordon identities”, arXiv:math/0006221 (2001).
376968.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0006221

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2000).

376982.title: Freeness conjecture for the equivariant cohomology of a graph
376982.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a graph with axial function $\alpha$, let $H(\Gamma,\alpha)$ be its equivariant cohomology ring, and let ${\mathbb S}({\mathfrak g}^*)$ be the polynomial ring occurring as the ring of constant maps. For a generic $\xi\in{\mathfrak g}$, let $\sigma_p$ be the number of ascending edges terminating at a vertex $p$, and let $b_k(\Gamma)$ be the number of vertices with $\sigma_p=k$. **Freeness conjecture.** $H(\Gamma,\alpha)$ is a free ${\mathbb S}({\mathfrak g}^*)$-module with $b_k(\Gamma)$ generators of degree $k$. This is one of the paper's Morse-theoretic conjectures concerning the equivariant cohomology ring of a graph; the supplied text gives no resolution status or further supporting context.
376982.source_name: Victor Guillemin and Catalin Zara, “Combinatorial formulas for products of Thom classes”, arXiv:math/0007166 (2000).
376982.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0007166

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2000).

376988.title: The flip-symmetric alternating sign matrix generating-function conjecture
376988.statement:
Let $F_n(x)$ be the weight-generating function for flip-symmetric alternating sign matrices, with the exponent recording the number of $-1$ entries in the first half of the columns. This symmetry class is empty unless the size is odd. Let $T_n(x,1)$ be the triangular-array generating function defined in the source. **Flip-symmetric generating-function conjecture.** It is conjectured that

$$
F_{2n+1}(x)=T_n(x,1).
$$

This proposes a refined enumeration of flip-symmetric alternating sign matrices by triangular arrays. The source gives no resolution status.
376988.source_name: David P. Robbins, “Symmetry Classes of Alternating Sign Matrices”, arXiv:math/0008045 (2000).
376988.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0008045

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2000).

376989.title: The half-turn-symmetric alternating sign matrix factorization conjecture
376989.statement:
Let $H_n(x,y)$ be the weight-generating function for half-turn-invariant $n$ by $n$ alternating sign matrices, and let $Z_n(x,y,0)$ and $Z_{n-1}(x,y,1)$ be the corresponding plane-partition generating functions defined in the source. **Half-turn factorization conjecture.** It is conjectured that

$$
H_{2n}(x,y)=Z_n(x,y,0)Z_{n-1}(x,y,1).
$$

The proposed factorization suggests a bijection between half-turn-symmetric $2n$ by $2n$ alternating sign matrices and the Cartesian product of $n$ by $n$ alternating sign matrices with cyclically symmetric plane partitions in the box ${\cal X}_n$. The formula is described as observed, and the source gives no proof or resolution.
376989.source_name: David P. Robbins, “Symmetry Classes of Alternating Sign Matrices”, arXiv:math/0008045 (2000).
376989.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0008045

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2000).

377044.title: The points-and-lines conjecture for free and K(pi,1) arrangements
377044.statement:
Let ${\mathcal A}$ be a hyperplane arrangement with underlying matroid $G$. The **points** of $G$ are its flats of rank one, and its **lines** are its flats of rank two. Saying that $G$ is determined by its points and lines means that the matroid structure is uniquely determined by these rank-one and rank-two flats.

**Points-and-lines conjecture.** The underlying matroid of a free or $K(\pi,1)$ arrangement is determined by its points and lines.

This conjecture would imply that the combinatorial structure of matroids underlying free or $K(\pi,1)$ arrangements is controlled by rank-one and rank-two data. The text connects it to Terao’s freeness conjecture and the matroidality of the homotopy type of arrangement complements, but supplies no resolution.
377044.source_name: Michael Falk, “Line-closed matroids, quadratic algebras, and formal arrangements”, arXiv:math/0010167 (2001).
377044.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0010167

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2000).

379148.title: Sundaram–Welker acyclicity conjecture for partition-poset complexes
379148.statement:
Let $\lambda$ and $\mu$ be different set partitions with $\lambda\vdash\mu$, and let $X_{\lambda,\mu}$ be the associated complex introduced in the paper. Here $\lambda\vdash\mu$ denotes the stipulated refinement relation between the set partitions.

**Sundaram–Welker's acyclicity conjecture.** For $\lambda\vdash\mu$ with $\lambda\neq\mu$, the space $X_{\lambda,\mu}$ is ${\mathbb Q}$-acyclic.

This is presented as equivalent to the original formulation concerning the multiplicity of the trivial representation in the stabilizer module on the reduced homology of the corresponding partition-poset interval. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
379148.source_name: Dmitry N. Kozlov, “Trends in Topological Combinatorics”, arXiv:math/0507390 (2005).
379148.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2001–2005). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:math/0111167](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0111167).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0507390

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2005).

381088.title: The graph characterization of generic minimal rigidity on concentric cones and tori
381088.statement:
Let ${\mathcal{M}}$ be a cone, a torus, a union of concentric cones or a union of concentric tori, and let $p$ be a generic placement. A graph $G$ is **generically minimally rigid** on ${\mathcal{M}}$ when the framework $(G,p)$ has generic minimal rigidity on ${\mathcal{M}}$. The graph $G$ is $(2,1)$-tight when it satisfies the corresponding $(2,1)$-tightness condition.

**Graph characterization conjecture.** Then $(G,p)$ is generically minimally rigid on ${\mathcal{M}}$ if and only if $G=K_{2}$, $K_3$, $K_4$, or $G$ is $(2,1)$-tight.

This conjecture would characterize generic minimal rigidity for frameworks on cones, tori, and unions of concentric cones or tori. The source presents it as further work expected to follow from the preceding inductive construction theorem; its resolution is not supplied here.
381088.source_name: Anthony Nixon and John Owen, “An Inductive Construction of (2,1)-tight Graphs”, arXiv:1103.2967 (2012).
381088.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.2967

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2011).
